name: שְׁאַלְתִּיאֵל
summary: Shealtiel son of Jeconiah, born in the captivity, father of Zerubbabel, the governor of Judah who led the return and built the altar and the house with Jeshua (1Ch 3:17; Ezr 3:2; 5:2; Hag 1:1). Both genealogies of Jesus pass through him and Zerubbabel (Mat 1:12; Luk 3:27, where he is son of Neri). The name is a sentence: שְׁאַלְתִּי “I have asked” and אֵל “God”, the father's word over a son given in answer, as Hannah said of Samuel, “from Yahweh I asked him (שְׁאִלְתִּיו)” (1Sa 1:20). Haggai writes it also shortened, שַׁלְתִּיאֵל.

evidence.note: “The sons of Jeconiah, the captive: שְׁאַלְתִּיאֵל his son.”
The same verb in the first person over a child given: “for from Yahweh I asked him (שְׁאִלְתִּיו)”.
“For this boy I prayed, and Yahweh gave me my request which I asked (שָׁאַלְתִּי) from him.”
“Zerubbabel son of שְׁאַלְתִּיאֵל, governor of Judah.”
“I will take you, Zerubbabel son of שְׁאַלְתִּיאֵל, my servant … and make you like a signet ring, for I have chosen you.”
Jeshua and Zerubbabel son of Shealtiel built the altar of the God of Israel.
In the Aramaic: “Zerubbabel בַּר שְׁאַלְתִּיאֵל” began to build the house of God.
“After the deportation to Babylon, Jeconiah begot Σαλαθιήλ, and Σαλαθιὴλ begot Zerubbabel.”
“… son of Zerubbabel, son of Σαλαθιὴλ, son of Neri.”

note: Takes v.ag.ah (Hebrew) and xv.aa.ac (the Aramaic of Ezr 5:2; that key also counts the Hebrew tokens a second time). People: TIPNR keeps Luke's Shealtiel son of Neri (Shealtiel@Luk.3.27) apart from Matthew's and Chronicles' son of Jeconiah; both are tagged, as one spelling. 1Ch 3:19 makes Zerubbabel son of Pedaiah, Shealtiel's brother, where the other books say son of Shealtiel: left to the reviewer. The gloss takes ־תִּי as the first person perfect with אֵל, as the full spelling shows; no verse explains the name.
